prompt: What can be granted to a principal in IAM?

choices.text: A single permission, such as `pubsub.topics.publish`
choices.why: There is no way to grant a permission on its own. It has to be in a role.

choices.text: A role, holding a set of permissions
choices.why: Right. A permission is never granted alone; it always arrives inside a role.

choices.text: A permission or a role, whichever is smaller
choices.why: Grants are made of roles. A custom role is how you get a small one.

choices.text: An API, enabled for that principal
choices.why: APIs are enabled per project, not per principal.

prompt: Read `resourcemanager.projects.delete` aloud. What does it allow?

choices.text: Deleting any resource inside a project
choices.why: The resource in the name is the project itself, not what it holds.

choices.text: Managing who may delete projects
choices.why: That would be a permission on IAM policies. This one is the deletion itself.

choices.text: Restoring a deleted project
choices.why: Restoring has a permission of its own, with the verb undelete.

choices.text: Deleting a project
choices.why: Right. The Resource Manager's projects, the verb delete.

prompt: A deployer was given Editor on the production project to update the website. What is the problem?

choices.text: It changes nearly everything else, too
choices.why: Right. Editor spans every enabled service, and it grows as Google adds services.

choices.text: Editor cannot deploy websites
choices.why: Editor can deploy the website. The trouble is everything else it can do.

choices.text: Editor lets the deployer grant roles to others
choices.why: Managing IAM is what Owner adds. Editor alone cannot grant roles.

choices.text: Editor expires after ninety days
choices.why: A grant has no expiry unless a condition gives it one.

prompt: Why does the number of Owners of a production project measure how many people can take it over?

choices.text: Owner is the only role that can read the project
choices.why: Viewer reads it too. What Owner adds is the IAM.

choices.text: Owners receive the project's bill
choices.why: The bill goes to the billing account, lesson 11.

choices.text: Owner grants any role, Owner included, to anybody
choices.why: Right. Holding Owner is holding the power to make anybody anything.

choices.text: Owner bypasses organisation policies
choices.why: Lesson 4: no role lifts a constraint, Owner included.

prompt: The planner's order service publishes to `orders` and does nothing else with Pub/Sub. Which predefined role fits?
hint: The working role in the middle of the ladder.

choices.text: `roles/pubsub.editor`
choices.why: Editor creates and deletes topics, which the service never needs.

choices.text: `roles/pubsub.admin`
choices.why: Admin also manages who may use the topics. Far too much.

choices.text: `roles/pubsub.publisher`
choices.why: Right. It publishes, and it cannot create, delete or consume.

choices.text: `roles/editor`
choices.why: The basic Editor role reaches every service in the project.

prompt: `roles/pubsub.publisher` is granted to the order service on the topic `orders` rather than on the project. What changes?

choices.text: It may publish to `orders` and to no other topic
choices.why: Right. The smaller the resource the grant is on, the smaller the mistake can be.

choices.text: Nothing, as roles are always project-wide
choices.why: Many services accept grants on single resources, and Pub/Sub is one.

choices.text: It may publish to every topic, but only from `orders`
choices.why: Publishing has no 'from'. The grant on `orders` covers `orders`.

choices.text: It also needs Viewer on the project to see the topic
choices.why: Publishing needs the publish permission on the topic, which the grant gives.

prompt: A security team must read every project in production. Where is its role granted?
hint: The smallest resource that spans the job.

choices.text: On each production project, one by one
choices.why: That works until next month's new project, which nobody remembers to add.

choices.text: On the organisation
choices.why: That reaches non-production and shared too, which the job does not need.

choices.text: On the billing account
choices.why: A billing account grants nothing on projects.

choices.text: On the folder `production`
choices.why: Right. The job spans projects, and the folder is the smallest node that holds them all.

prompt: A role granted a year ago now lets its holder use a feature that did not exist then. Is that a bug?
hint: How do predefined roles change over time?

choices.text: Yes: a grant's permissions are frozen when it is made
choices.why: That is how a custom role behaves, not a predefined one.

choices.text: No: Google adds new permissions to predefined roles
choices.why: Right. Predefined roles grow by addition, so a grant can allow more than it did on the day it was made.

choices.text: Yes: the role must have been changed to a custom one
choices.why: A custom role would not have gained the permission at all.

choices.text: No: grants are renewed every year with the latest role
choices.why: Grants are not renewed; the role they name changed underneath.

prompt: For production grants, prefer roles whose launch stage is ___ rather than BETA or ALPHA.
Match each Pub/Sub role to its job.

hint: Compare with the rules for a project id.

choices.text: A role id takes no hyphen
choices.why: Right. Letters, digits, underscores and full stops, three to sixty-four of them.

choices.text: A role id must start with `roles/`
choices.why: `roles/` begins predefined roles' names. A custom role's full name is written by Google.

choices.text: The id is longer than sixty-four characters
choices.why: It has fourteen. The character is the problem, not the length.

choices.text: Google already has a role with that id
choices.why: `validate` asks Google nothing; it checked the form.

prompt: Where can a custom role be defined?
hint: Two of the four levels of the tree.

choices.text: On any node: organisation, folder or project
choices.why: Folders are the one level that cannot hold custom roles.

choices.text: On a single resource, such as one topic
choices.why: A role can be granted on a resource, but it is defined on the organisation or a project.

choices.text: On the organisation or on a project
choices.why: Right. Never on a folder: a role meant for many projects is defined on the organisation.

choices.text: On the billing account, so it can be charged
choices.why: Roles cost nothing and do not live on billing accounts.

prompt: Six months after writing a custom role for the reports job, the job is refused for a permission Pub/Sub added last week. What happened?
hint: Does a custom role grow on its own?

choices.text: Custom roles expire after six months
choices.why: They last until somebody deletes them.

choices.text: The custom role did not gain it; somebody has to add it
choices.why: Right. Predefined roles grow with the service, custom roles stay as written.

choices.text: Google removed a permission from the role
choices.why: Google does not edit custom roles. It is the missing new one.

choices.text: The grant moved to the predefined role by itself
choices.why: Grants never move. The custom role is still what the job holds.

prompt: The plan for the custom role passes. At apply, Google refuses one of its permissions. How can that be?
hint: Each permission has a support level the provider does not know.

choices.text: The provider forgot to send it
choices.why: The plan shows every permission, and the apply sends them all.

choices.text: Custom roles take only one permission each
choices.why: A custom role may hold thousands.

choices.text: The stage was `GA`, which forbids new permissions
choices.why: The stage is a label for people; it forbids nothing.

choices.text: That permission is not supported in custom roles
choices.why: Right. Some are `NOT_SUPPORTED` in custom roles, and only Google knows which.

prompt: A custom role is deleted by mistake. For how many days can it be restored?
The reports job needs to consume from one subscription and list topics. A colleague proposes `roles/pubsub.editor` on the project, 'to be safe'. What is the better grant?

choices.text: `roles/pubsub.editor` on the project, as proposed
choices.why: Editor creates and deletes topics and subscriptions, which the job never does.

choices.text: `roles/viewer` on the organisation
choices.why: Viewer cannot consume messages, and the organisation is far too wide.

choices.text: `roles/owner` on the subscription only
choices.why: Owner on anything lets its holder grant roles there.

choices.text: A narrow role, granted where the job works
choices.why: Right. 'To be safe' with Editor means the job can delete every topic. Narrow is the safe choice.
